newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't calls on alcohol sector to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't calls on alcohol sector to cut costs.

text.p: Brazil's government called on the domestic alcohol sector to cut costs and raise efficiency in order to pave the way for the abolition of government subsidies to the sector.
"The time has come for a contribution from the sector," Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Britto told a seminar on the alcohol sector in Brasilia.
"This is a system of subsidies which is not transparent," he said.
Brazil officially opened up its anhydrous alcohol sector on May 1 this year and is working towards liberalising the rest of the market including sugarcane and hydrous alcohol by May 1998.
Costs could be cut by eight percent for the industrial sector and 22 percent for the agricultural sector using currently available technology, Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles said.
In exchange he pledged the government would work to eliminate trade barrriers against Brazilian exports of sugar and alcohol in the international markets.
